description: Map the nine Mandaic bowls of Morgenstern 2012's preliminary survey to their editions. Five are edited in Morgenstern, 'Five Mandaic Magic Bowls from the Moussaieff Collection', Eretz-Israel 34 (2021): 106-122 (source SRC-553965D06B17); the rest in Morgenstern and Abudraham, 'Additional Mandaic Magic Bowls from the Moussaieff Collection', Mehqarim be-Lashon (Hebrew; listed as forthcoming on the author's page, reported elsewhere in the corpus as 2025). Seven survey identities are unlinked in TEXT-001: M23, M25, M26, M139, M154 and unnumbered A and B. Obtain the tables of contents or first pages before linking any bowl.
resolution_notes: Opened 2026-09-27 by Claude Code. No paper-to-object mapping could be verified from open metadata. 2026-09-27: JSTOR's first-page preview of Morgenstern 2021 (stable 27165940) shows the first edition is Moussaieff 23 (= survey M23, now linked) and says Moussaieff 25 and 158 are NOT in the article but reserved for a planned book on Mandaic bowls in private collections. The other four bowls need pp. 107-122 (free 'Read online' with a JSTOR account, or Library of Congress African & Middle Eastern Reading Room, call number DS108.9 .E74 2015 Hebr, v. 34, onsite only). 2026-09-27 (later): read the whole article on JSTOR through Mike's account. Its five bowls are Moussaieff 23 (p. 106), 24 (p. 109), 26 (p. 112), 139 (p. 114) and 154 (p. 118); each matches the survey record and is merged and linked. Still unlinked: M25 (reserved, with M158, for a planned book on Mandaic bowls in private collections), M45 and unnumbered A and B (presumably Morgenstern–Abudraham, 'Additional Mandaic Magic Bowls', Mehqarim be-Lashon, forthcoming). Open question: JSTOR's indexed text of the 2012 chapter begins 'Twelve Mandaic Magic Bowls in the Moussaieff Collection', while the corpus records nine; check the chapter's own count.

description: Kedar 2019 states that ten bowls were unpublished when she wrote: JNF 18, JNF 125, JNF 149, JNF 152, JNF 153 and JNF 188 ('unpublished texts by James Nathan Ford', p. 134 n. 546), Wolf 69 and CBS 85-48-914 (p. 105 n. 434), Wolf 23 (p. 135) and Davidovitz 2 ('being prepared for publishing by James Nathan Ford', p. 102 n. 410). Check Ford's and others' publications since 2019 (Ford published JNF 124 in 2016 and Davidovitz 41 in 2023). Any bowl still unpublished could become the corpus's first sourced no-known-edition finding, but a 2019 statement is dated evidence: decide the policy before recording one.
resolution_notes: Opened 2026-09-27 by Claude Code. No no-known-edition finding recorded. 2026-09-27 ruling (Mike): a 2019 'unpublished' statement is not current evidence and must not be recorded as a no-known-edition finding. Keep these ten bowls as follow-up targets for future publication searches.

description: Three identities appear to describe National Library of Israel Heb. 4° 6079 (the Scholem bowl): IBI-0B59840825F5 (Naveh–Shaked 1985 Bowl 12a, p. 188), IBI-56CB143F21AA ('JNL Heb 4, 6079' in Kedar 2019, p. 134 n. 546, now linked to Amulets and Magic Bowls) and IBI-032BEDEB7102 (NLI catalogue Ms. Heb. 6079=34). Review them together with the Scholem identity lead under CONC-003; no merge was made.
resolution_notes: Opened 2026-09-27 by Claude Code. RESOLVED 2026-09-27: Mike ruled that records sharing one institution-scoped designation are one bowl unless there is evidence they differ; none was found. Recorded in research/reviews/researcher_identity_decisions_2026-09-27.jsonl. The meaning of the NLI catalogue's '=34' suffix remains unverified.

description: Scope-review Montgomery, 'A Syriac Incantation Bowl with Christian Formula', AJSL 34 (1918): 137-139, which very probably edits the one Hyvernat bowl (IBI-EA02F6D6DE6D). The volume is pre-1930 US and freely readable on JSTOR; JSTOR, the publisher DOI and Internet Archive were unreachable from the 2026-09-27 session. Once scoped, link the Hyvernat bowl.
resolution_notes: Opened 2026-09-27 by Claude Code. RESOLVED 2026-09-27: read in full on JSTOR through Mike's Chrome; scoped as a single-bowl edition and the Hyvernat bowl linked.
